According to the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Apple reportedly considered a feature for Apple Upgrade that would make setting up a new iPhone almost seamless: Apple would pre-copy your data to the new device. However, the feature never saw the light of day.

The concept is simple: since consumers upgrade their devices every so often through fixed monthly installments, why not make the transfer process as simple as possible? Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports:

There were evidently some issues. First, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, since the data transfer could only happen when the device is shipped, leaving a lag of several days — unless you choose to pick it up in store.

In addition, there are obvious privacy concerns. If you're backing up to iCloud, it shouldn't be surprising that Apple has your data. But for the general public, there might be concerns about how the data gets transferred to the new phone, and worries about whether anyone might peek at the data during the process.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a new system in its stores called Presto, which lets employees update an iPhone while it's still in the box. One can imagine this system could have been extended to support iCloud backup transfers, without anyone ever needing to look at your data.

Still, the feature never came to fruition — and that might be for the best.
